LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 5.3.1 ADJECTIVES

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.3: Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Adjectives
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Adjectives, part of Strand 5 in Grade 6 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Which words do we use to describe people, things, and places? 2. How do we compare people, things, and events?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify simple, comparative and superlative forms of adjectives in print and digital texts correctly,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Adjectives in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use simple, comparative and superlative forms of adjectives in oral and written texts,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Adjectives in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. acknowledge the importance of using adjectives correctly in communication.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Adjectives in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify simple, comparative and superlative forms of adjectives in print and digital texts correctly,

   Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Adjectives helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. use simple, comparative and superlative forms of adjectives in oral and written texts,

   Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Adjectives helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. acknowledge the importance of using adjectives correctly in communication.

   Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Adjectives helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. identify adjectives in print and digital texts,

2. compare items using simple, comparative and superlative forms of adjectives,

3. collaborate with peers to make a list of regular and irregular adjectives,

4. create a crossword puzzle and a word search, using comparative and superlative adjectives,

5. display the completed crossword puzzle and word search on posters or charts. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. identify adjectives in print and digital texts,
2. compare items using simple, comparative and superlative forms of adjectives,
3. collaborate with peers to make a list of regular and irregular adjectives,
4. create a crossword puzzle and a word search, using comparative and superlative adjectives,
5. display the completed crossword puzzle and word search on posters or charts. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Adjectives together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-efficacy: The learner’s ability to plan efficiently is developed as they create and display the crossword puzzles

and word search.

• Digital Literacy: The learner’s ability to manipulate digital devices is improved as they share work accomplished

(crossword puzzles and word search) on posters and charts.

Values:
Respect: This is inculcated as the learner collaborates with peers to make a list of regular and irregular adjectives while

respecting diverse opinions.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Safety and Security: The learner’s sense of security is promoted as the he/she learns about safety when interacting

with animals and when they visit various tourist attraction sites.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to apply the knowledge of adjectives which are a key aspect in the grammar lessons in Kiswahili.

Main points to remember:

1. identify simple, comparative and superlative forms of adjectives in print and digital texts correctly,
2. use simple, comparative and superlative forms of adjectives in oral and written texts,
3. acknowledge the importance of using adjectives correctly in communication.
